input.quote: Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Contractor shall provide to Company, and hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.
input.rationale: Section 6 (Termination) addresses only termination notice, payment of Contractor's accrued fees, and assignment of Works in progress. It contains no post-termination transition assistance, no obligation to return Company data or Confidential Information, and no deletion/certification requirement. Section 4 (Ownership) establishes that Works are Company property and Section 8 restricts use of Confidential Information, but neither creates any return, export or destruction obligation on exit — a targeted search for "return", "transition", "export", "delete", "destroy" and "migrat" returned no results anywhere in the agreement. On a services/development engagement where Contractor holds Company records, data and Works, this absence is a deviation warranting insertion. The proposed new Section 6(c) tracks the preferred position (six months of assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, return within thirty days in machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter) and uses the agreement's existing defined terms ("Works", "Confidential Information") for consistency. Fallback of ninety days' assistance is offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and certified deletion obligations in Section 6 (Termination).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 6 covers notice and final fees but says nothing about exit: we have no right to wind-down help and no assurance our data and Confidential Information come back or are deleted. We have added a new Section 6(c) giving us up to six months of transition assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is an issue, we can accept ninety days of assistance provided the thirty-day export and deletion certificate remain.

ops.text: (c) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Statement of Work for any reason, Contractor shall (i) at Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Contractor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiry or termination, return to Company all Works, Confidential Information and other Company data and materials then in Contractor's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete all such Confidential Information, data and materials from its systems and certify such deletion to Company in writing.
